newsitem.title: USA: CBOT to announce venture with Liberty, Prebon.
newsitem.headline: CBOT to announce venture with Liberty, Prebon.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade will soon announce a joint venture with two brokerages, Liberty Brokerage Investment Corp and Prebon Yamane (USA), regarding the CBOT's Chicago Board Brokerage (CBB) system, exchange sources said Wednesday.

"Between the exchange, Liberty and Prebon, they will set up an electronic platform to trade U.S. government cash bonds, and later all types of derivatives," one exchange source close to the negotiations said.
Chicago Board Brokerage, an electronic trading system owned by the CBOT, received U.S. regulatory approval last year to trade cash U.S. Treasury securities.
"They (the CBOT and the brokerages) would like to have the electronic system up an running by the middle of 1997," the source said.
The CBOT said it planned a news conference on Thursday to announce a joint strategic venture with Liberty and Prebon, but a CBOT spokesman declined to elaborate.
Ann Gorski, marketing director for both Liberty and Prebon, had no comment.
With CBB, exchange members and member firms will have direct access to trade cash T-bonds, T-notes and T-bills on both an outright and a when-issued basis.
Trades will be cleared by the Clearing Corp for Options and Securities, a subsidiary of the Board of Trade Clearing Corp, the CBOT's independent clearinghouse.
One industry official who worked closely on the CBB negotiations said the venture would still require member approval. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
